- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast is below recent highs, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is above recent lows, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast to avoid overshoot.  
- Model consistently underestimates true values after a recent spike in sentiment (e.g., after 0.93+ sentiment), especially in the 10–15 day horizon.  
- Forecast often lags true price movements by 2–4 days, especially when sentiment is volatile — adjust for 1–2 day lag in forward-looking models.  
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — model tends to push prices back toward historical mean too aggressively, especially when sentiment is neutral or declining.  
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes (e.g., 0.93+ followed by 0.87+) are common — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak to avoid overcorrection.  
- In low-sentiment environments (≤0.2), model often ignores downward pressure — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day to reflect subdued market sentiment.
